items.stem: What does it mean that NotebookLM is 'source-grounded'?

options.text: Its answers are based on the sources you add to the notebook
options.rationale: Correct: responses draw on the added sources with citations.

options.text: It answers from the open web by default
options.rationale: It grounds in your added sources, not the open web by default.
Citations are central to its grounding.

options.text: It trains a model on your documents permanently
options.rationale: Grounding is retrieval, not permanent training.

items.explanation: Correct: answers are grounded in the sources you add.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Why should you open the citation behind a NotebookLM answer?

options.text: To confirm the answer matches the source passage
options.rationale: Correct: citations let you verify the answer against the source.

options.text: To add a new source automatically
options.rationale: Opening a citation does not add sources.

options.text: To remove the answer from history

items.explanation: Correct: citations let you verify the answer against its source.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are appropriate uses of NotebookLM? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Summarising and querying a set of documents you added
options.rationale: Correct: it is built for querying your sources.

options.text: Generating study aids grounded in your sources
options.rationale: Correct: briefings and FAQs are grounded study aids.

options.text: Answering questions about topics with no added source
options.rationale: Without a source it cannot ground the answer.

items.explanation: Correct: query and study your added sources.
